title: CBDT Chairman Shri Ravi Agrawal inaugurates Taxpayers' Lounge at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), 2026, celebrating the spirit of Vikas aur Virasat
subtitle:
CBDT releases 18 informative brochures and a children's book introducing basics of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes
Senior Citizens' Helpdesk introduced this year; immersive installations and interactive games make taxpayer awareness engaging for visitors of all ages
body_text:
Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), today inaugurated and dedicated the Taxpayers' Lounge at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), 2026, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, to the general public from 13th to 27th November, 2026. Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT, along with senior officers, marking the formal opening of the Taxpayers' Lounge at Hall No. 4, Bharat Mandapam. Spread across an expansive 507 sq. metres, the Taxpayers' Lounge brings alive the spirit of Vikas aur Virasat , blending India's rich cultural heritage with contemporary technology and immersive experiences. The Lounge reflects the evolution of India's tax administration and the Department's vision of a progressive, transparent and citizen-centric tax ecosystem. Its key attractions include: Triveni Kinetic LED: The Lounge's digital centerpiece, combining movement, light and dynamic visual storytelling to symbolise the convergence of tradition, technology and transformation. It is complemented by a Kar-Sathi Holobox that interacts with visitors and answers their queries. Tree of Life: At the heart of the Lounge stands the Tree of Life, whose deep, timeless roots symbolise Virasat – India's heritage, enduring values and collective good. The Archway of Growth represents the nation's journey of progress and aspirations, while the Canopy of Hope signifies protection, inclusivity and collective well-being, conveying how responsible taxation contributes to nation-building. Heritage-inspired entrance: The entrance draws inspiration from the iconic Toran of the Sanchi Stupa, reimagined in a contemporary design language. Symbolising auspicious beginnings, it marks the dawn of a new era of tax reforms under the Income-tax Act, 2025. The two pillars at the entrance carry the Department's guiding motto on one side and 'Prarambh – The New Income-tax Act, 2025' on the other. Dynamic LED Fascia: A running LED fascia across the Lounge gives it a vibrant digital identity, showcasing key messages and departmental initiatives. Interactive experiences: Digital and VR games on the theme of Income Tax, including 'Little Bee: Big Nation' , VR bowling, along with Nukkad Natak , magic shows and quizzes, make taxpayer awareness engaging for visitors of all ages. The Tree of Life installation at the heart of the Taxpayers' Lounge. Among other things, the Lounge also offers dedicated taxpayer services through six helpdesks providing assistance on: e-Filing of returns and related queries PAN and PAN-related services Use of the AI Chatbot Grievance redressal through CPGRAM International Taxation A Senior Citizens' Helpdesk, introduced for the first time this year As part of its knowledge and awareness initiatives, the Department released 18 informative brochures on taxpayer services, along with a specially designed children's book that introduces the fundamentals of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes, promoting early tax awareness and financial literacy among the next generation. The Income Tax Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 (13–27 Nov), was dedicated to the general public today by Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman CBDT, in the presence of other senior officers of the Department.  

Spread across an expansive 507 sq. metres, the Pavilion brings alive the spirit of “Vikas Aur Virasat”, blending India's rich cultural heritage with contemporary technology and showcasing the Department’s journey towards a trust-based and citizen-centric tax ecosystem.   

Key attractions include: 

🔹 Triveni Kinetic LED: A digital installation symbolising the convergence of tradition, technology and transformation, complemented by a Karsathi Holobox to engage with visitors and answer their queries.  

🔹Tree of Life: A specially designed installation symbolising heritage, enduring values, sustainable growth and the contribution of responsible taxation to nation-building.  

🔹Interactive experiences for kids and adults:  Digital and VR games, including 'Little Bee: Big Nation' and VR bowling, along with Nukkad Natak, magic shows and quizzes.   

🔹Dedicated taxpayer helpdesks: Six helpdesks to provide guidance on e-Filing, PAN, AI Chatbot, grievance redressal (CPGRAM), International Taxation and a specially introduced Senior Citizens' Helpdesk. 

🔹Knowledge and awareness initiatives: Release of 18 informative brochures and a specially designed children's book introducing the fundamentals of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes, promoting early tax awareness and financial literacy.

The Pavilion reflects the Income Tax Department's commitment to ease of compliance, citizen engagement and nation-building, rooted in India's rich heritage and empowered by technology. 

Visitors are invited to explore the Pavilion and experience its diverse range of interactive activities, exhibits and taxpayer services, offering an engaging and informative experience for people of all age groups. — Income Tax India (@IncomeTaxIndia) November 16, 2026 **** KT/KMN
